record.provider: Digital Research Alliance of Canada — 1 TB default object storage per project, up to 40 TB project / 100 TB nearline via Rapid Access Service

free_tier.stated: 'All Arbutus projects are allocated a default 1TB of object storage. If more is required, you can either request an additional 9TB available through our Rapid Access Service. More than 10TB must be requested and allocated under the annual Resource Allocation Competition.' The RAS policy adds: PIs 'can request additional storage resources in any General Purpose cluster without submitting a RAC application, up to a maximum of 40 TB of project storage and 100 TB of nearline storage', with the total across all clusters capped at those numbers.

egress.terms: Unmetered egress. OpenStack Swift and S3 interfaces serve objects over HTTPS, and buckets can be configured for public read access.

record.tooling: OpenStack Swift or S3 against the Arbutus object store; rclone/swift/s3cmd all work. 'We offer access to the OpenStack Object Store via two different protocols: Swift or Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3). ... object storage containers and objects created with Swift or S3 can be accessed using both protocols.'
record.chaining: Allocation provides 1 TB default, 9 TB via Resource Allocation Competition, and up to 40 TB project storage per principal investigator upon email request. Nearline tape storage provides up to 100 TB.

limits.value: application, up to a maximum of 40 TB of project storage and 100 TB of nearline storage', w

record.limits_note: Per-object-cap: not documented for Arbutus. Retention: object storage is not backed up. 'management of a project's object storage containers is self-service. This includes operations such as backups because the object store itself is not backed up.' request-rate: not published. Gate: CCDB account (institutional), and storage above 10 TB requires an email to support@tech.alliancecan.ca from a PI.

identity_cost.detail: an account is registered on the CCDB portal. The Principal Investigator role that requests the storage is an academic PI: a full- or part-time faculty member, an adjunct faculty member, or a librarian at a Canadian university, college or research hospital eligible to hold Canada Foundation for Innovation grants; a lead researcher at an eligible Canadian research institute is the second route, and industry, non-profit and government researchers apply for paid access through a regional organisation. A sponsored user needs no affiliation of their own but 'require a sponsor to create an account on CCDB'. No card and no phone number is asked for.

free_tier.stated: Canada's national platform ran about 233,000 CPU cores, 62,000 virtual CPUs, 2,610 GPUs and 150 PB of storage across Cedar, Graham, Niagara, Beluga and Arbutus. It reserves "a target of 20% for researchers to use through the Rapid Access Service (RAS), which grants all users access to modest quantities of compute, storage and cloud resources as soon as they have a Compute Canada account", against 80% allocated competitively.
